shell-task.ask.label: The agent's question
shell-task.ask.setupNote: Nothing changes unless you allow it. Or type why not below.
shell-task.held.title: Held: {label}
shell-task.held.harness: {name} changed since wisp last ran it
shell-task.held.withoutTip: The agent runs with your own settings only: not the repo’s hooks or its MCP servers, and a new worktree’s setup doesn’t run
shell-task.held.trustAsks: This repo asks to run its own programs
shell-task.held.trustChanged: This repo’s hooks, servers or setup changed since you trusted it
shell-task.held.trustWhy: Held before it started: these would run on this computer, as you, whatever the mode.
shell-task.held.setupRunning: Trusted. Running the repo’s worktree setup; the run starts when it’s done.
shell-task.halt.signedOutWhy: Sign in and this turn runs again.
shell-task.changed.limit: A possible cause, not proof: a change on the provider's side wouldn't show here.
shell-task.delegations.title: Delegated agents
shell-task.receipt.cacheTip: {pct} of what it read came from the cache
shell-task.receipt.overage.extraTip: Billed as extra usage: the plan’s windows were used up, so the provider charged this run on top
shell-task.receipt.overage.creditsTip: Billed to your Codex credits: the plan’s windows were used up, so this run took credits
shell-task.receipt.overage.apiTip: Billed to an API key, not your plan: Claude Code found an API key (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or an apiKeyHelper) and used it
shell-task.receipt.overage.profileTip: Billed to a Claude Console org, not your plan: Claude Code ran on a Console profile, which it uses when the claude.ai login has ended or ANTHROPIC_PROFILE names one. claude auth login signs back in to the plan
shell-task.halt.handTip: Sends the same prompt to {name}, with this task's turns
shell-task.halt.handTipModel: Sends the same prompt to {name} on {model}, with this task's turns
shell-task.halt.noTarget: No agent on another company’s model is set up to take it. Add one in Settings → Agents, or rephrase it in the reply box.
shell-task.halt.waiting: Carries on at {at}, after the reset
shell-task.pr.none: This task has no pull request.
shell-task.pr.fixing: The agent is resolving the conflicts
shell-task.pr.draft: Draft: merging marks it ready first
shell-task.pr.needsReview: Needs a review before it can merge
shell-task.pr.mergeAsk.title: Merge this pull request?
shell-task.pr.mergeAsk.body: It squash-merges on GitHub and updates your local base branch. The task's worktree is removed after, unless it holds work the merge doesn't take (uncommitted changes, or commits the pull request doesn't have): then it stays, and you're told.
shell-task.shell.unsupported: No shell on Windows yet: wisp’s terminal needs macOS or Linux on the computer the task runs on.
shell-task.changes.vsTitle: Compared with {base} where this branch left it, uncommitted changes included
shell-task.changes.seenTitle: Not a git diff: the edits wisp saw the agent make
shell-task.changes.openFileTitle: Open any file of this task in the editor
shell-task.changes.viewedOn: Viewed: untick to review it again
shell-task.changes.viewedOff: Mark as viewed: folds it until its diff changes
shell-task.changes.revertTitle: Put this change back as it was before the task
shell-task.changes.stagedTitle: {n} of {total} changed files staged: Commit takes those
shell-task.changes.allTitle: Nothing staged: Commit stages all {n} changed files first
shell-task.changes.revertAsk.title: Revert {path} to {base}?
shell-task.changes.revertAsk.changed: Every change this task made to {name} goes. Undo puts it back.
shell-task.changes.revertAsk.new: {name} is new in this task, so reverting deletes it. Undo brings it back.
shell-task.changes.revertAsk.deleted: {name} comes back as it was before the task. Undo puts it back.
shell-task.preview.intro: Run the app from this task’s folder and see it here.
shell-task.preview.needCommand: Type the command that starts the app, then Run.
shell-task.preview.guessed: From the project: its run setting or package.json’s script. Change it if it isn’t right.
shell-task.comment.hint: ⌘↵ to keep it · it goes with your next follow-up
shell-task.comment.waiting.one: {count} comment goes with your next follow-up
shell-task.comment.waiting.other: {count} comments go with your next follow-up
shell-task.preview.pickTitle: Pick element: click one in the page to describe it in the reply box
shell-task.preview.pickWait: Pick element (once the page has loaded)
shell-task.watch.none: Nothing to watch on this task.
shell-task.watch.copyRun: Copy the command, with cd into its folder
shell-task.files.placeholder: Find a file or text in this task’s folder…
shell-task.files.empty: This task’s folder has no files yet
shell-task.files.noGit: Open file… needs a git folder: this task’s isn’t one
shell-task.file.label: {path}: edit, then Save (⌘S)
shell-task.file.ask: Ask about it: the file (or the lines selected) goes in the reply box
shell-task.file.noDefinition: No definition of {name} in this folder
shell-task.shell.endAsk.title: End the shell?
shell-task.term.endAsk.title: End the terminal?
shell-task.shell.endAsk.body: Whatever runs in it stops with it.
